clues.text: This city is the capital of a state in southern India. It sits on an east coast beside the Bay of Bengal.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside the east coast of southern India

source.quote: Chennai, also known as Madras, is the capital and largest city of Tamil Nadu, the southernmost state of India. It is located on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal.

clues.text: Most of its rain falls in one season, brought by the north-east monsoon winds. That time of year often brings cyclones, and low ground floods under the rain.
clues.narrowing: narrows to the part of that coast where the north-east monsoon brings the main rains and floods

source.quote: It receives most of the rainfall from the Northeast monsoon with cyclones being common features during the season, resulting in water inundation and flooding in low-lying areas.

clues.text: In 1639, the British got this coast by a land grant. They built Fort Saint George, the first British fort in India.
clues.narrowing: shortlists the Indian coast cities founded from a 1639 British land grant and first fort

source.quote: In 1639, the British East India Company obtained a grant for a strip of coastal land which then contained the fishing village of Madrasapattinam. The British developed the Madras port and built Fort St. George, the first British fortress in India.

clues.text: People come from far away for care at its hospitals. Many call it the health capital of India.
clues.narrowing: near-decisive for players who know the Indian city famed for medical travel

source.quote: It is a major centre for medical tourism and is termed "India's health capital".

clues.text: This city is called the Cultural Capital of South India. It is a big centre for music, art, and dance.
clues.narrowing: confirms the South Indian cultural capital known for music, art, and dance

source.quote: Chennai is a major centre for music, art and dance and is called the Cultural Capital of South India.

clues.text: This city in Minnesota sits on both banks of the Upper Mississippi River. It sits near the east side of the state.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside Minnesota and the upper Mississippi River area

source.quote: Located in the state's center near the eastern border, it occupies both banks of the Upper Mississippi River and adjoins Saint Paul, the state capital of Minnesota.

clues.text: Winters here are cold and snowy, but summers turn hot and wet. The seasons swap from one hard extreme to the other.
clues.narrowing: rules out places in the region with mild winters or cool summers

source.quote: Minneapolis is built on an artesian aquifer on relatively flat terrain and is known for cold, snowy winters and hot, humid summers.

clues.text: Dakota people lived here first. Settlers then built by a fort and the lone falls on the great river, whose power helped the town grow.
clues.narrowing: rules in river towns that grew by a fort and a falls; rules out most other river cities

source.quote: Dakota people previously inhabited the site of today's Minneapolis. European settlement began north of Fort Snelling along Saint Anthony Falls—the only natural waterfall on the Mississippi River. Location near the fort and the falls' power—with its potential for industrial activity—fostered the city's early growth.

clues.text: This is the birthplace of Target, General Mills, and the Pillsbury brand. Three names seen on food and store shelves began here.
clues.narrowing: rules in the birthplace of those food and store brands; nearly decisive

source.quote: the city is the birthplace of General Mills, the Pillsbury brand, Target Corporation, and Thermo King mobile refrigeration.

clues.text: This place is called the City of Lakes. It has thirteen lakes and a park road that links its parks and green spots.
clues.narrowing: confirms a lake-rich city on the upper river; converts remaining guessers

source.quote: Nicknamed the "City of Lakes", Minneapolis is abundant in water, with thirteen lakes, wetlands, the Mississippi River, creeks, and waterfalls. The city's public park system is connected by the Grand Rounds National Scenic Byway.
